catalog.title: Courses
catalog.intro: ISRD courses apply the Learner-First Systemic Education framework — each course is designed to shift the learner's mental model, not just deliver content. Courses combine article-based exposition, interactive simulations, AI-facilitated dialogue, and transfer challenges across real-world domains.
catalog.approach_note: Every course is built on the Learner-First Systemic Education framework. Before content is introduced, your current mental model is surfaced. Simulations let you discover dynamics directly. AI tutoring probes whether the new model is operational. Transfer challenges test whether understanding generalizes.

tracks.label: Foundations
tracks.description: Core concepts in systems science and systemic thinking — the intellectual foundation for all ISRD work.

tracks.label: Learner-First ID

tracks.label: Bio-Systemics

courses.title: Introduction to Learner-First Systemic Education
courses.subtitle: How to design instruction that actually shifts mental models
courses.description: An introduction to the Learner-First Systemic Education framework — the ISRD approach to instructional design for complex domains. Covers attractor theory applied to learning, the seven-phase module structure, AI tutoring architecture, and simulation as an epistemological tool. Includes hands-on design exercises using ISRD simulation tools.

modules_preview.title: The Attractor Problem in Learning
modules_preview.desc: Why traditional instruction fails complex domains and what attractor theory reveals about persistent misconceptions.

modules_preview.title: Phase 1–2: Surfacing and Perturbation
modules_preview.desc: How to reveal the learner's current mental model and introduce productive instability.

modules_preview.title: Phase 3–4: Exposition and Simulation
modules_preview.desc: Minimal structural exposition followed by direct simulation-based exploration.

modules_preview.title: Phase 5: AI-Facilitated Reflection
modules_preview.desc: Designing the pedagogical context for AI Socratic dialogue — goals, misconception library, adaptive scaffolding.

modules_preview.title: Phase 6–7: Transfer and Integration
modules_preview.desc: Cross-domain transfer challenges and explicit course graph navigation.

modules_preview.title: Course as Feedback System
modules_preview.desc: Designing the dependency network connecting course modules and modeling the learner's attractor trajectory.

modules_preview.title: Applied Design Project
modules_preview.desc: Design a complete Learner-First Systemic Education module for a complex domain of your choice.

courses.title: Introduction to Systems Science
courses.subtitle: The four eras of systems thinking and why they matter now
courses.description: A ground-up introduction to systems science — from General Systems Theory through cybernetics, complexity science, and the AI era. Each era is explored through interactive simulations and AI-facilitated reflection. Includes the Feedback Loops, Lorenz Attractor, and Emergence simulations.

courses.title: Post-Viral Illness as a Complex System
courses.subtitle: Understanding ME/CFS and chronic conditions through attractor dynamics
courses.description: A systems-based course for clinicians, patients, and researchers working with post-viral and treatment-resistant conditions. Uses the ME/CFS Population Outbreak Simulator and brainstem ANS model as learning instruments. Applies Learner-First Systemic Education design throughout.

lessons.title: What Is Systems Science?
lessons.description: Systems science is the study of pattern — the structures and principles that recur across every domain, from feedback loops to attractors to emergence.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley

lessons.title: Feedback Loops
lessons.description: The circular causality that makes system behavior counterintuitive — reinforcing and balancing loops, delay, and why feedback is the engine of dynamic behavior.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley

lessons.title: Emergence
lessons.description: Why the whole exceeds the sum of its parts — attractors, hierarchy, and self-organization as the mechanisms behind emergent behavior.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley

lessons.title: General Systems Theory
lessons.description: Bertalanffy's interdisciplinary study of systems in general — boundary, wholeness, hierarchy, isomorphism, and equifinality as the ontological foundation of systems science.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley

lessons.title: Module 1: Foundations and Core Concepts
lessons.description: What is a system, boundary and environment, open versus closed systems, wholeness, and equifinality.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley

lessons.title: Module 2: System Properties and Behavior
lessons.description: Hierarchy, feedback, nonlinearity, and isomorphism — the GST toolkit for analyzing system behavior.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley

lessons.title: Cybernetics
lessons.description: The science of control and communication in systems — feedback control loops, first and second order cybernetics, and how systems regulate themselves.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley

lessons.title: Complexity Science
lessons.description: Complex adaptive systems, emergence, self-organization, the edge of chaos, and attractor landscapes — from the Santa Fe Institute tradition.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley

lessons.title: Systems Dynamics
lessons.description: Forrester's method for modeling dynamic systems — stocks, flows, causal loop diagrams, and the classic models that built the field.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley

lessons.title: Systems Practice
lessons.description: An integrated toolkit — diagnose, model, intervene, evolve — for applying all four foundation theories together across any domain.
lessons.author: Kurt Rowley
